title: Ciguatera
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Seventeen-year-old Yusuke Ogino is bullied at school along with his friend Takai, and his only hope is getting a motorcycle. At driving school he meets Yumi, who becomes his first girlfriend, and the story follows him and his classmates through high school and into working life with pitch-black humor and bleak realism.
life_message: A good life is finding small footholds of love and self-respect in a world that does not care much what young people do to each other.

content.note: Bullying beatings described as 'bloody and bruised' (ANN); MangaUpdates tags violence, kidnapping and attempted murder.
Reviewers call it bleak and 'uncomfortable' (ANN); MangaUpdates tags dark ambience and a psychopath character.

Teen romance and sexual themes: classmate Sakazuki sexually harasses and blackmails Ogino, transactional sex implied (ANN); MangaUpdates tags rape, attempted rape and sexual coercion; nudity (AniList, MangaUpdates). Non-graphic detail to verify.
Severe school bullying; a friend seems close to bringing a gun to school (ANN); MangaUpdates and AniList tag bullying.
Bullying, blackmail and lying shown among teens (ANN; MangaUpdates blackmail and liar tags).
Motorcycle dream as escape; no product focus noted.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Bullied boys get no help from teachers or rules and must endure or escape alone (MangaUpdates, ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Ogino's hope is personal freedom on a motorcycle (AniList, MangaUpdates).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Friendship and romance matter more than family; family not described in sources.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: School pecking order rules teen life; no respected elders shown (to verify).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Secular, modern setting; no religious frame.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival through bullying with a wish for self-expression and love.

folkways.japan: Group bullying (ijime) and the pressure to endure quietly reflect real concerns in Japanese schools, shown as context.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers say its message lands only 'to a degree' and was 'shooting for something more profound'; none call it preachy.
delivery.note: The bleak worldview is shown through events and art rather than stated.

winners_losers: Ogino survives and grows somewhat through love and chance rather than effort (ANN); bullies are not clearly punished, and the story's sympathy stays with the bullied.
